items.title: 18.10.2 Reaction of Manganate(VII) Ion with Iron(II) Ion

source_refs.note: Topic 18.10.2 (PDF 34). The printed E of -0.77 V, the E cell of +2.29 V and the overall equation are corrected (Quick Check 18.8 itself gives +0.77 V). Flagged for review.

blocks.text: In this reaction MnO4- is reduced and Fe2+ is oxidised. The half-reactions, written as reductions, are:

MnO4- has the more positive E, so it is reduced, and Fe2+ is oxidised. Five Fe2+ ions supply the five electrons one MnO4- ion needs: MnO4- + 8H+ + 5Fe2+ -> Mn2+ + 5Fe3+ + 4H2O. E cell = E(reduction) - E(oxidation) = 1.52 - 0.77 = +0.75 V. The positive value shows the reaction is feasible.

blocks.title: Slips in the printed working
blocks.text: The book prints E for Fe3+/Fe2+ as -0.77 V, adds the two values to get E cell = +2.29 V, and writes the overall equation as MnO4- + 5Fe2+ -> Mn2+ + 5Fe2+ + 4H2O. Its own Quick Check 18.8 gives +0.77 V. The lesson uses +0.77 V, E cell = +0.75 V, and the balanced equation with 8H+ and 5Fe3+.

blocks.prompt: How many moles of Fe2+ react with one mole of MnO4-?
blocks.explanation: Five: each MnO4- gains five electrons and each Fe2+ gives one.
